title: Chapter 1 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of Getting Started with Next.js concepts!

questions.question: What is the main problem with plain React’s default rendering approach?
options: It renders everything on the client, causing slow initial loads and poor SEO
It can only run on Node.js
questions.explanation: Plain React (CRA) uses Client‑Side Rendering, sending an empty HTML shell. The browser must load JavaScript before content appears, harming SEO and perceived performance.

questions.question: Which Next.js feature automatically creates routes based on files in the `pages/` directory?
questions.explanation: Next.js uses the file‑system as the router. Any `.js`/`.jsx`/`.tsx` file inside `pages/` becomes a route.

questions.question: What command is used to create a new Next.js app?
questions.explanation: The official way is `npx create-next-app@latest`. It scaffolds a new project with all the necessary defaults.

questions.question: Which folder is used to serve static assets like images directly?
questions.explanation: Files inside `public/` are served as static assets by Next.js. You can reference them with a `/` path (e.g., `/logo.png`).

questions.question: What does the `Link` component from `next/link` do that an `<a>` tag does not?
options: Performs client‑side navigation without a full page reload
questions.explanation: `Link` enables SPA‑like transitions, prefetching pages and avoiding a full browser refresh.

questions.question: Next.js pages must be written as class components.
questions.explanation: You can write pages as function or class components, but function components with Hooks are the modern standard.

questions.question: The `_app.js` file can be safely deleted if you don't need global styles.
questions.explanation: `_app.js` is required. It initializes pages and allows you to add global CSS, layouts, and state providers. Removing it breaks the app.

questions.question: Next.js can only generate pages on the server, never statically.
questions.explanation: Next.js supports both Static Generation (SSG) and Server‑Side Rendering (SSR). It can also incrementally regenerate static pages (ISR).

questions.question: In the build output, what does a hollow circle (○) signify?
questions.explanation: ○ indicates a page that was statically generated at build time (no server needed at runtime).

questions.question: What is the purpose of `npm run dev`?
options: Start a development server with hot reload
questions.explanation: `npm run dev` launches the Next.js development server with Fast Refresh, allowing instant preview of code changes.

questions.question: Which command creates an optimized production build?
questions.explanation: `npm run build` compiles the application, applies optimizations, and pre‑renders pages for production.

questions.question: The file `pages/index.js` automatically maps to the route _____.
questions.explanation: `index.js` inside any folder corresponds to the root of that path. In `pages/`, it becomes the homepage `/`.

questions.question: To navigate between pages without a full reload, import the ______ component from 'next/link'.
questions.explanation: The `Link` component enables client‑side transitions. You import it using `import Link from 'next/link'`.

questions.question: What is the output folder after a successful production build?
questions.explanation: Next.js outputs the production build to the `.next` folder.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a built‑in feature of Next.js?
questions.explanation: Next.js does not come with a built‑in state management library. You can use any React state management like Redux or Context.

questions.question: Next.js can only be deployed to Vercel.
questions.explanation: Next.js can be deployed to any Node.js hosting platform, including AWS, Netlify, Docker, etc., though Vercel provides the best integration.

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of Static Generation (SSG)?
options: HTML is generated at request time
Pages are pre‑built and can be served from a CDN, making them extremely fast
questions.explanation: SSG pages are rendered at build time and can be cached globally on a CDN, offering the fastest possible performance.

questions.question: In Next.js, where do you place background images or other static files?
questions.explanation: The `public/` directory is the root for static assets. Files like `public/logo.png` can be used with `<Image src="/logo.png" />`.

questions.question: Which script in `package.json` starts the production server after a build?
questions.explanation: After `npm run build`, you run `npm start` to serve the optimized production build.

questions.question: How does Next.js handle TypeScript?
options: It has built‑in TypeScript support with zero configuration
Only API routes can use TypeScript
questions.explanation: Next.js provides first‑class TypeScript support. Just add `tsconfig.json` and rename files to `.tsx`.

questions.question: In Next.js, every page must export a React component as the default export.
questions.explanation: Each page file must have a `export default function` (or class) that renders the page content.

questions.question: Why is Next.js often described as 'the React framework for production'?
options: It provides all the tooling needed to build, optimize, and scale React applications
It removes the need for JavaScript
questions.explanation: Next.js gives you routing, rendering strategies, optimization, API routes, and deployment solutions out of the box, making it ideal for production‑ready apps.

questions.question: When you run `npm run dev`, what happens when you edit and save a page?
options: You must manually refresh the browser
questions.explanation: Next.js development server uses Fast Refresh, which instantly reflects code changes in the browser while preserving component state.

questions.question: Which statement about the `pages/_app.js` file is true?
options: It's used to define the homepage
It wraps every page and is the ideal place for global CSS and layouts
It's optional and only needed for CSS modules
It only runs on the server
questions.explanation: `_app.js` is the custom App component. It persists across page changes and is the top‑level component for state, global styles, and layouts.
